recommendedTextbook.title: A Guide to WASSCE/SSCE Literature-in-English
recommendedTextbook.author: Kola Eke
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: NERDC & Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education

topics.topic: Shakespearean Drama: Elizabethan Theatre and Tragic Heroics
subtopics: Prescribed Shakespearean tragedy (e.g. Macbeth, Hamlet, Othello): Elizabethan theatrical conventions and worldview (Great Chain of Being)
The tragic hero: Noble birth, hamartia (fatal flaw), peripeteia (reversal of fortune), anagnorisis (recognition), catharsis
Themes: Ambition, supernatural solicitation, appearance vs reality, destiny and free will
objectives: Identify Elizabethan social beliefs reflected in Shakespeare's supernatural elements
Trace the tragic protagonist's psychological degeneration through dramatic soliloquies
Explain the concept of tragic catharsis in classical dramatic criticism

topics.topic: Non-African Poetry: Metaphysical and Romantic Traditions
subtopics: Prescribed British and American poems (e.g. John Donne, William Wordsworth, T.S. Eliot, Maya Angelou)
Metaphysical conceits, romantic pantheism, modern alienation, and civil rights resistance
Metrical analysis: Iambic pentameter, blank verse, free verse, enjambment, caesura
objectives: Analyze a metaphysical conceit comparing spiritual love to a compass
Scan lines of poetry to identify iambic rhythm and metric variations
Evaluate how Romantic poets turn to untouched nature as a sanctuary from industrialization

topics.topic: Unseen Prose and Unseen Poetry Appreciation
subtopics: Techniques for tackling unseen literary comprehension in WAEC/NECO Paper 1 and Paper 2
Isolating tone, mood, atmosphere, and attitude of the persona in unfamiliar verse
Evaluating thematic concerns, syntax choices, and figures of speech under exam conditions
objectives: Determine persona attitude (sarcastic, nostalgic, celebratory, mournful) from linguistic clues
Analyze an unseen 14-line sonnet and identify its octave/sestet turn (volta)
Score full marks on the unseen literary analysis section of WAEC examinations

topics.topic: Comparative Literary Synthesis and WAEC Examination Masterclass
subtopics: Comparative essay writing: Synthesizing themes across African and Non-African prescribed texts
WAEC Chief Examiner marking rubric (Content, Organization, Expression, Mechanical Accuracy)
Avoiding plot narration: Structuring analytical, thesis-driven critical responses
objectives: Structure a comparative essay contrasting female agency in African vs Western literature
Apply the WAEC marking scheme rubric to grade student practice essays
Eliminate plot summary habits and write high-scoring critical literature answers
